005package org.wpilib.hardware.discrete;
006
007import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.PWMJNI;
008import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.SimDevice;
009import org.wpilib.internal.UnitTelemetry;
010import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryLoggable;
011import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryTable;
012import org.wpilib.units.Units;
013import org.wpilib.util.UsageReporting;
014
015/**
016 * Class implements the PWM generation in the FPGA.
017 *
018 * <p>The values supplied as arguments for PWM outputs range from -1.0 to 1.0. They are mapped to
019 * the microseconds to keep the pulse high, with a range of 0 (off) to 4096. Changes are immediately
020 * sent to the FPGA, and the update occurs at the next FPGA cycle (5.05ms). There is no delay.
021 */
022public class PWM implements TelemetryLoggable, AutoCloseable {
023  private final int m_channel;
024
025  private int m_handle;
026
027  /**
028   * Allocate a PWM given a channel.
029   *
030   * <p>Checks channel value range and allocates the appropriate channel. The allocation is only
031   * done to help users ensure that they don't double assign channels.
032   *
033   * @param channel The SmartIO channel number.
034   */
035  public PWM(final int channel) {
036    m_channel = channel;
037
038    m_handle = PWMJNI.initializePWMPort(channel);
039
040    setDisabled();
041
042    UsageReporting.reportUsage("IO", channel, "PWM");
043  }
044
045  /** Free the resource associated with the PWM channel and set the value to 0. */
046  @Override
047  public void close() {
048    if (m_handle == 0) {
049      return;
050    }
051    setDisabled();
052    PWMJNI.freePWMPort(m_handle);
053    m_handle = 0;
054  }
055
056  /**
057   * Gets the channel number associated with the PWM Object.
058   *
059   * @return The channel number.
060   */
061  public int getChannel() {
062    return m_channel;
063  }
064
065  /**
066   * Set the PWM value directly to the hardware.
067   *
068   * <p>Write a microsecond pulse value to a PWM channel.
069   *
070   * @param microsecondPulseTime Microsecond pulse PWM value. Range 0 - 4096.
071   */
072  public final void setPulseTimeMicroseconds(int microsecondPulseTime) {
073    PWMJNI.setPulseTimeMicroseconds(m_handle, microsecondPulseTime);
074  }
075
076  /**
077   * Get the PWM value directly from the hardware.
078   *
079   * <p>Read a raw value from a PWM channel.
080   *
081   * @return Microsecond pulse PWM control value. Range: 0 - 4096.
082   */
083  public final int getPulseTimeMicroseconds() {
084    return PWMJNI.getPulseTimeMicroseconds(m_handle);
085  }
086
087  /** Temporarily disables the PWM output. The next set call will re-enable the output. */
088  public final void setDisabled() {
089    setPulseTimeMicroseconds(0);
090  }
091
092  /**
093   * Sets the PWM output period.
094   *
095   * @param millisecondPeriod The output period to apply to this channel, in milliseconds. Valid
096   *     values are 5ms, 10ms, and 20ms. Default is 20 ms.
097   */
098  public void setOutputPeriod(int millisecondPeriod) {
099    int scale =
100        switch (millisecondPeriod) {
101          case 5 -> 0;
102          case 10 -> 1;
103          case 20 -> 3;
104          default -> 3; // default to 20ms if invalid value is given
105        };
106
107    PWMJNI.setPWMOutputPeriod(m_handle, scale);
108  }
109
110  /**
111   * Get the underlying handle.
112   *
113   * @return Underlying PWM handle
114   */
115  public int getHandle() {
116    return m_handle;
117  }
118
119  /**
120   * Indicates this input is used by a simulated device.
121   *
122   * @param device simulated device handle
123   */
124  public void setSimDevice(SimDevice device) {
125    PWMJNI.setPWMSimDevice(m_handle, device.getNativeHandle());
126  }
127
128  @Override
129  public void logTo(TelemetryTable table) {
130    UnitTelemetry.log(table, "Value", getPulseTimeMicroseconds(), Units.Microseconds);
131  }
132
133  @Override
134  public String getTelemetryType() {
135    return "PWM";
136  }
137}
